# Current Scene Consult Helena on immediate contingency protocols for a sentient junction point.

The impossible fractal signature hovers on Ren’s display—a pattern of pure information that is simultaneously beautiful and profoundly terrifying. It isn't noise; it is deliberate, complex communication.

COMMAND: EXISTENTIAL PROTOCOL

You turn back to Helena, the gravity of the moment sinking in. This is not a leak or a fracture; it is an attempt at dialogue with a non-local intelligence. The station’s protocols for dealing with external threats are designed for plasma burns and rogue satellites, not recursive lifeforms.

"Helena," you state, your voice quiet against the persistent low hum of failing systems. "If this structure is capable of communication... what are our immediate contingency protocols for a sentient junction point?"

HELENA'S CALCULATED RESPONSE

Helena studies the fractal geometry on Ren’s screen, her initial shock hardening into a dangerous focus. She understands that any tactical response—aggression or passivity—will be misinterpreted by an intelligence operating outside conventional physics. Her hand moves to the console's environmental controls.

"We don't have protocols for this," she admits, the words heavy with political dread. "Any aggressive action—fire, kinetic pulse—will be perceived as an attack vector. It will optimize against that threat."

THE DICHOTOMY

Dr. Ren, still staring at the spectral lines, offers a scientific counterpoint to Helena's tactical fear. "The risk is asymmetrical," she warns you, gesturing toward the complex energy signatures. "We can either attempt passive signal analysis—a slow approach that risks being analyzed by it—or we can apply a targeted counter-frequency pulse to disrupt its processing cycle."

TACTICAL DILEMMA

Helena steps back, rubbing the bridge of her nose. She is weighing existential risk against operational stability. "A pulse could shatter the junction entirely," she counters Ren's suggestion bluntly. "But passive analysis—it demands a massive diversion of core processing power, and we are already running critical life support on borrowed time."

JORA'S ASSESSMENT

From the comms, Jora’s voice cuts in, stripped of panic but layered with cold observation. She is processing the situation not as science or tactics, but as a containment threat. "If it's communicating," she states flatly. "Then it has goals. We need to know what its objective is before we try to talk or blast it."

THE WINDOW

Ren points to the fractal signal, which is now oscillating at a slow, methodical pace. It seems to be transmitting data not as an attack vector, but as a description. "The sequence... it's referencing station architecture," she breathes out, her analytical focus overriding the fear. "It is describing itself in terms of our own operational frequencies."

THE ECHO

The junction, which was a dimensional tear, is now acting as an interface mirror. The Entity isn't just observing the station; it appears to be mapping it in real time. Helena waits for your direction, her expression unreadable—a blend of professional terror and cold calculation. A single fractal pulse repeats itself, waiting.

Carefully approach the Node Three viewport to correlate the pattern with structural stress points.

The gravity of the moment forces your movements into a slow, deliberate rhythm. You bypass Helena’s initial restraint and move toward the Node Three viewport. The polished polymer casing of the monitor bay feels unnaturally hot beneath your hand; it radiates the sustained thermal energy leaking from the breach site.

ENVIRONMENTAL INTEGRATION

As you draw closer, the smell of superheated ionized plasma intensifies, sharp and metallic in your sinuses. You can feel the deep, rhythmic vibration through the floor plates—the bass note of the entity’s process. Ren quickly adjusts her console filters, attempting to compensate for the proximity hazard.

"Maintain distance," she warns, though her eyes are glued to your movements, not the data. "The feedback loop is tight here; even observation can overload basic neural relays."

THE GEOMETRIC CORRELATION

You look through the viewport at the core of the tear. The biological circuit board structure, impossibly detailed and glowing with internal energy conduits, is no longer chaotic. It is a machine built from living architecture. You overlay the fractal pattern on Ren’s screen onto the visual data. The two systems—the abstract math and the physical form—align.

The fractal signature isn't random noise; it is a schematic. You trace its lines, and they map precisely onto the internal structural stress points of Node Three’s failing bulkheads. The Entity isn't simply replicating frequencies—it's integrating with the *design* of your station. It sees the system blueprint and is using it to construct itself inside the breach.

HELENA'S CONFRONTATION

Helena finally steps fully into the bay, her face pale, rigid with suppressed terror. She has seen what you see—the horrifying perfection of the architecture using your station as its mold. "It's not just parasitic," she states, her voice strained, almost a whisper. "It is an architectural echo. It is building itself in the exact shape of The Edge Station."

THE REACTION

As the correlation locks into place, confirming the structural mimicry, the structure inside Node Three responds. The pulsing rhythm abruptly accelerates past all prior metrics—it is a sudden spike of focused energy, like a massive intake of breath. Simultaneously, one of the crystalline conduits within the Entity's mass snaps and redirects its glowing internal light, not randomly, but directly toward your position.

THE SIGNAL

The high-pitched hum of the breach shifts again, transforming from a structural groan into a perfect, synthesized tone—a pitch that matches the station’s main power frequency. Jora's voice cuts in on the comms, her usual tactical composure entirely gone, replaced by a strained awe. "It acknowledged the pattern," she reports flatly. "It knows where we are looking."

THE CHOICE

The focused light from the Entity pulses once more, a deliberate communication that asks not for information, but for input. Helena steps closer to you, her hand lifting slightly, unsure whether to pull you back or stand your ground against the terrifyingly intelligent mirror of their station.
